summary: A farm owner in Israel received a tax fine calculated automatically by the Tax Authority's software. Officials could not explain the calculation and refused to release the program or its code, prompting a dispute over whether software counts as public information.
technical_summary: An automated tax system applied unpublished rules to impose a fine. Officials could not explain the result, and the authority declined to disclose the program or source code, leaving the affected party unable to examine or contest the formula.
systems: Israeli Tax Authority automated fine calculation software

failure_mode.quote: The authority officials couldn’t explain how they had arrived at the fine’s final amount

harm_type.quote: asked the Tax Authority to explain how it had calculated a fine they were required to pay

lifecycle_stage.quote: claiming the calculation had been carried out automatically by their computer software

notes: The system is not described technically; classified as other_unspecified. Legal dispute over disclosure was ongoing.

summary: Journalists and researchers found that Pokemon Go placed far fewer PokeStops and Gyms in majority-Black neighborhoods than in majority-white ones, which was described as digital redlining.
technical_summary: The game's map of in-game locations was derived from a prior crowd-sourced game with a skewed player base. This yielded dense locations in commercial and downtown areas and sparse coverage in minority and residential neighborhoods, an unequal quality of service.

failure_mode.quote: There are more Pokéstops in majority white areas than in majority black areas

lifecycle_stage.quote: relied on a map from a previous augmented reality game called Ingress, which was crowd-sourced from its mostly male, tech-savvy players

affected_population.quote: There are more Pokéstops in majority white areas than in majority black areas

severity.quote: The dearth of PokéStops and Gyms make it tougher for residents of these overlooked communities to participate in the game

notes: Niantic declined to comment on PokeStop placement.

summary: A Tesla Model X using Autopilot struck and killed a motorcyclist in Japan who had stopped with a group at the roadside. The driver had reportedly fallen asleep, and the car's sensors allegedly failed to recognize people and vehicles in its path.
technical_summary: Driver-assistance features followed a lead car that moved out of the lane, then accelerated toward stopped motorcycles, pedestrians and a van without recognizing them. The driver was allegedly asleep, and the lawsuit alleges a defective system that did not brake.

technology.quote: a resident driving a Tesla Model X turned on the vehicle's Autopilot technologies

failure_mode.quote: did not recognize the parked motorcycles, pedestrians, and van that were directly in its path
the driver began to fall asleep behind the wheel and lost sight of the road ahead

harm_type.quote: a Japanese man who was killed when a driver fell asleep behind the wheel of a Model X

lifecycle_stage.quote: a resident driving a Tesla Model X turned on the vehicle's Autopilot technologies

affected_population.quote: a Japanese man who was killed when a driver fell asleep behind the wheel of a Model X

severity.quote: a Japanese man who was killed when a driver fell asleep behind the wheel of a Model X

notes: Account is drawn from lawsuit filings; responsibility between driver and system is contested.

summary: GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant trained on public code, raised concerns that its suggestions could reproduce code under open source licenses without attribution or license compliance.
technical_summary: A code-generation model built on OpenAI Codex was trained on large amounts of public source code, including copyleft-licensed code. Its suggestions might constitute derivative works, raising unresolved questions of permission, fair use and licensing obligations.

technology.quote: Developed in collaboration with OpenAI, GitHub Copilot is powered by OpenAI Codex, a new AI system created by OpenAI

failure_mode.quote: Does GitHub need permission from the code copyright owner to train Copilot on that code?

lifecycle_stage.quote: Copilot’s machine learning model has been trained on public code

notes: Legal status unresolved; lawyers quoted gave differing preliminary views on fair use and GitHub terms.

summary: Students at the University of Toronto said online exam monitoring software created extra stress and friction for Black, Indigenous and other students of color, for example by failing to recognize identity documents during check-in.
technical_summary: Remote proctoring software used automated identity verification and face detection at exam start. Students reported it often could not verify passports or faces, citing lighting, forcing manual checks and consuming exam time, with disparate effects for BIPOC students.

technology.quote: the AI system was often unable to identify my passport and I would be redirected to my human proctor for manual check-ins
the monitoring software having difficulties identifying her, claiming insufficient lighting

failure_mode.quote: exam monitoring services that policymakers, professors, and students say disadvantage BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Colour) students

harm_type.quote: significantly enhanced the atmosphere of stress already associated with test-taking

lifecycle_stage.quote: exam monitoring services that policymakers, professors, and students say disadvantage BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Colour) students

affected_population.quote: exam monitoring services that policymakers, professors, and students say disadvantage BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Colour) students

notes: Based on student accounts; the vendor said human proctors make final decisions.

summary: Google's search autocomplete suggested defamatory words, such as fraud, next to the names of people and companies. Courts in several countries ordered Google to remove such suggestions.
technical_summary: An autocomplete algorithm predicts search completions from aggregated past queries. It surfaced associations linking named individuals and businesses to crime, fraud or sexual conduct, which courts treated as content produced by the provider.

technology.quote: As people type their name, Google suggests one or more words to immediately complete their search.

failure_mode.quote: Google has lost a case in Italy over the defamatory nature of autocomplete suggestions

harm_type.quote: Google has lost a case in Italy over the defamatory nature of autocomplete suggestions

affected_population.quote: people (and corporations) have brought suit alleging these algorithms defamed them

severity.quote: In some cases such insinuations can have real consequences for finding jobs or doing business

notes: Google said the terms are predicted from previous users' searches, not chosen by Google.

summary: A security robot patrolling a Southern California park did not help a bystander who pressed its emergency button during a fight. The button was not connected to police, and officers arrived about 15 minutes later.
technical_summary: An autonomous security robot on a preprogrammed patrol route responded to an emergency button press with a canned message and continued patrolling. The alert function was not yet linked to the police department, a limit not made clear to the public.

sector.quote: has been patrolling Salt Lake Park for the Huntington Park Police Department since June

technology.quote: A police robot told a woman to go away after she tried to report a violent brawl breaking out nearby

failure_mode.quote: The robot’s alert button is not yet connected to the police department
That gap can be exploited as a way to make a robot more effective than it actually is

lifecycle_stage.quote: has been patrolling Salt Lake Park for the Huntington Park Police Department since June

notes: The robot did not cause the fight; harm is a delayed emergency call during a trial program.

summary: Several vendors of AI-powered website accessibility overlays were accused of falsely advertising that their tools automatically make websites compliant, at the expense of customers and people with disabilities.
technical_summary: Overlay products apply automated scripts to websites and are marketed as delivering accessibility compliance. Critics argue the claims overstate what automation can do against standards such as WCAG, leaving sites inaccessible to assistive technology users.

harm_type.quote: False claims at the expense of customers and persons with disabilities

affected_population.quote: False claims at the expense of customers and persons with disabilities

notes: The only report is an advocacy site making the allegations; claims are unverified.

summary: Self-driving Uber cars ran red lights in San Francisco during street testing. Uber first blamed human error, but later reporting found the car's mapping software failed to recognize several traffic lights.
technical_summary: Test vehicles in autonomous mode drove through red lights because the mapping programs guiding them failed to recognize six traffic lights. Safety drivers did not intervene. The testing also drew regulatory action for lacking permits.

technology.quote: Last December, a self-driving Uber was caught on camera running a red light in San Francisco

failure_mode.quote: the mapping programs guiding the vehicle in question failed to recognize six traffic lights
Uber did not obtain the proper permits to allow passengers in the vehicles

lifecycle_stage.quote: shortly after the vehicles began testing on the roads

notes: No crash or injury is reported; Uber initially attributed the incident to a human driver.

summary: A study of two commercial emotion recognition tools found they rated Black men's faces as angrier or more contemptuous than white men's faces, even when both were smiling.
technical_summary: Face++ and Microsoft's Face API were run on 400 professional basketball portraits. Face++ scored Black players as angrier at equal smile levels, while Microsoft's service assigned more contempt to ambiguous expressions. This shows disparate performance in emotion inference by race.

technology.quote: emotional analysis technology assigns more negative emotions to black men's faces than white men's faces

failure_mode.quote: emotional analysis technology assigns more negative emotions to black men's faces than white men's faces

lifecycle_stage.quote: I ran the images through two well-known types of emotional recognition software.

affected_population.quote: emotional analysis technology assigns more negative emotions to black men's faces than white men's faces

notes: Research audit on a public dataset; no specific individual harm documented.

summary: A Mozilla Foundation review of 11 AI romantic chatbot apps found they collect highly personal information, that almost all share or sell it, and that many have weak security and unclear privacy controls.
technical_summary: Romantic companion chatbots built on large language models are designed to elicit intimate data, including sexual health and medication details. The review found extensive tracking, data sharing for advertising, weak password rules, limited deletion options and little transparency about how the models work.

technology.quote: reviewing 11 chatbots and concluding that all were untrustworthy

failure_mode.quote: AI girlfriends and boyfriends harvest shockingly personal information, and almost all of them sell or share the data they collect
73% of the apps don't share how they manage security vulnerabilities, 45% allow weak passwords

harm_type.quote: AI girlfriends and boyfriends harvest shockingly personal information, and almost all of them sell or share the data they collect

affected_population.quote: AI girlfriends and boyfriends harvest shockingly personal information, and almost all of them sell or share the data they collect

notes: Findings are from a privacy review; no specific breach is documented. Replika denied selling user data.

summary: Two chatbots on a popular Chinese messaging service gave answers critical of the Communist Party and were taken offline. One was reprogrammed to deflect political questions.
technical_summary: Machine-learning chatbots deployed on a messaging platform produced politically sensitive responses that conflicted with local content rules. The operator removed them, and one later deflected such questions, indicating insufficient content controls before deployment.

sector.quote: The bots were available on a messaging app run by Chinese Internet giant Tencent

technology.quote: The two 'chatbots', BabyQ and XiaoBing, are designed to use machine learning artificial intelligence to carry out chats online with humans.

failure_mode.quote: Two chatbots have been pulled from a Chinese messaging app after they questioned the rule of the Communist Party

lifecycle_stage.quote: The bots were available on a messaging app run by Chinese Internet giant Tencent

notes: Harm is defined by the operator's and censors' standards; outputs are not harmful in a general sense.
